title: Check twisted-state spectra on Kuramoto cycle networks
domain: Dynamics on networks and collective behavior
statement: For the simple undirected cycle C_n, n >= 3, consider theta_dot_j = sin(theta_(j-1)-theta_j) + sin(theta_(j+1)-theta_j), with indices modulo n and phases modulo 2 pi. Reproduce the equilibrium and Jacobian spectrum for theta_j = 2 pi q j/n, 0 <= q <= floor(n/2), and classify linear stability modulo uniform rotation. Build an exact sign table only for 3 <= n <= 20. Extra zero eigenvalues must be labeled inconclusive for nonlinear stability. The finite range is curator chosen.
source_locator: Townsend et al., equations (4)-(5) and Section II.1; McRae, Section 1.2
status_basis: The spectrum is a known result in the opened paper. Later work preserves the distinction between second-order criticality and nonlinear stability. No table or simulation has been produced by this project.
plain_summary: A ring of identical oscillators supports synchronized and twisted phase patterns. A known spectrum provides a compact test of instability, stability up to common rotation, and cases where linearization cannot decide.
assumptions: Use a simple undirected cycle, n >= 3, identical frequencies removed by a rotating frame, and unit positive edge coupling.
The phase ODE has no noise, delay, inertia or frequency heterogeneity.
Commonly rotated configurations represent the same relative-phase state.
Use the dynamics Jacobian; a potential-Hessian sign convention must be translated explicitly.
scope: Reproduce the general cycle formula, then classify signs only for 3 <= n <= 20 and 0 <= q <= floor(n/2). Other graphs, all-equilibrium classification and nonlinear degenerate-case analysis are outside scope.
target: The known spectral derivation, exact finite sign certificates and an explicit treatment of rotational symmetry.
success_criteria: Verify that the proposed twisted configuration is an equilibrium for the stated edges.
Recover J_q = -cos(2 pi q/n) L_Cn and eigenvalues 2 cos(2 pi q/n)(cos(2 pi r/n)-1), r = 0,...,n-1.
Separate the rotational zero eigenvalue from any additional zeros.
Justify finite-table signs exactly, without treating near-zero floating values as certificates.
A positive eigenvalue establishes instability. All nonrotational eigenvalues negative support asymptotic stability modulo rotation; extra zeros remain inconclusive for nonlinear stability.
known_results: The source supplies the twisted equilibria and circulant Jacobian, including the nearest-neighbor cycle specialization.
Rotational symmetry contributes a necessary zero mode.
Later work distinguishes second-order critical points from stable nonlinear equilibria.
prerequisites: Smooth ODE linearization and stability modulo symmetry.
Exact trigonometric signs or certified algebraic-number calculations.
significance: Creates a transparent baseline for network stability studies and prevents local numerical spectra from being mistaken for global synchronization proofs.

relations.explanation: Cycle spectra prepare local-stability methods used in connectivity studies, but do not settle the dense-network threshold or nonlinear degenerate cases.

requirements.experiment: None for the idealized ODE calculation. Physical or biological comparisons require separate observations or experiments.
requirements.data: Cycle edges, n and q; no empirical time series.
requirements.compute: Symbolic differentiation and matrices of order at most twenty for the finite table. Exact trigonometric reasoning avoids numerical optimization. The bounds are chosen for inspectability; no runtime, cost or success rate has been measured.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Homogeneous first-order phase coupling on a fixed unweighted undirected cycle. Unequal frequencies, amplitude dynamics, noise and delays are outside this model.

ai_assessment.rationale: The known formula and a bounded exact table independently check symbolic reasoning and symmetry handling without relying on trajectories as proof.

clarity.reason: The ODE, equilibria, spectral target and finite range are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Equilibrium checking, differentiation, diagonalization and sign classification are separate.

methods.reason: The paper gives an explicit formula and standard circulant-matrix methods.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Differentiation and exact signs suit symbolic tools.

checkability.reason: The analytic formula and small cases allow independent review.

expertise.reason: A dynamics reviewer must handle the symmetry quotient and degenerate cases.

significance.reason: This is a verification baseline rather than a new synchronization result.

verification_difficulty.reason: The algebra is compact, but a wrong stability interpretation would overstate the result.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No model calculation or simulation has been tested. Degenerate cases intentionally receive no nonlinear verdict.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes a tool-using AI that can read mathematical sources, produce inspectable symbolic work and code, and work with a human domain reviewer.

obstacles: Incorrect cycle edge counting at small n.
Dropping or misinterpreting the rotational zero mode.
Rounding an exact zero into a positive or negative value.
Inferring global synchronization from selected twisted equilibria.

steps: Check adjacency and derivative signs against the ODE.
Independently derive the Jacobian and compare it with the Laplacian.
Check Fourier eigenvalues and exact finite sign certificates.
Review every stability label and the limits for extra-zero cases.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate: short symbolic work is inspectable, but local, orbital and global behavior require dynamics expertise.
validation.statement_alignment: The result concerns only the stated twisted equilibria. It is not an all-equilibrium classification, empirical prediction or global synchronization guarantee.

known_attempts: Townsend, Stillman and Strogatz analyze these spectra in the literature. No independent atlas computation or AI trial is recorded.
unresolved_checks: Select a representation for exact trigonometric signs before implementation.
Have a reviewer approve terminology for asymptotic stability modulo rotation.

attribution.citation: Townsend, A., Stillman, M., and Strogatz, S. H. (2020 version), Dense networks that do not synchronize and sparse ones that do, arXiv:1906.10627v4, Section II. Later context: McRae, A. D. (2026 version), arXiv:2503.18801v2, Sections 1.2 and 3.4.

status_search.limitations: This known-result calibration does not resolve degenerate nonlinear dynamics. Later-work searches are not a complete audit of all graph families.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: The spectrum and conditional stability labels concern the homogeneous phase model with the stated symmetry convention.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: The calculation does not establish behavior of measured physical, biological or social networks.
